text:
sara: seeing a p99 jump after the 03:12 deploy, digging in. p50 fine, but p99 up ~3x for the small-text workloads :eyes:

mike: can you paste the top-level traces? any change in kernel selection or microbatch sizes?

sara: pasted the relevant snippets below. early guess: tool-call chains are causing repeated KV cache misses + a kernel recompile path getting triggered for some sequences.

sara: PERF OUTPUT (sampling, 30s window):
```
KernelPick: {fastpath: 68%, fallback_quant: 22%, recompile: 10%}
KVCache: {hit: 82%, miss: 18%}
MicrobatchSizeHistogram: {1:12%,2:18%,4:30%,8:25%,16:15%}
TailRequests: tool_call_loop: 14% of p99 events
```

ana: that 10% recompile is worrying. which condition triggers recompile? long seq? new attention pattern?

kevin: recompile usually fires when kernel heuristics see atypical layout — e.g., long prompt + repetitive tool args that break fastest kernel tiling. I bet the tool calls produce extremely long single-token expansions causing different tile sizes -> recompile.

mike: also look at KV eviction traces. if tool calls repeatedly flush prefix entries, that raises cost on next requests and can push requests into fallback paths (higher latency).

sara: KV trace snippet: `evict_count: 430 / 120s, avg_kv_size: 1.2MB, top-evicters: tool-runner (62%)`

infra-bot: deploy 03:12 -> rollout 100% completed 03:18 (sha: a1b2c3) :white_check_mark:

ana: can we reproduce? suggestions: replay a set that includes nested tool-call traces and long prompts, with microbatch_size=8 and batching_window_ms=10. try setting kernel_pin=true (disable recompile) to see if p99 improves.

sara: reproduction plan:
1) replay: ./tools/replay_trace --trace trace_2026-03-16-toolloop.json --rate 150
2) set ENV: REDWOOD_MICROBATCH=8, BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10, KERNEL_PIN=true
3) collect perf + pprof: ./bin/collect_perf --out /tmp/p99-run

mike: quick query I ran on metrics: `sum_over_time(requests{route="small-gen"}[$__range]) by (kernel_choice)` shows spike in fallback_quant during the window.

kevin: short-term mitigation: increase batching window to 20ms for small-gen routes (trades latency for fewer kernel switches), or force kernel_pin for dedicated customers experiencing this.

ana: long-term: adjust kernel-selection heuristic to consider recent KV eviction rate and toolcall markers so we don't recompile mid-tail. maybe add a smoothing factor over 30s.

sara: I'll run the repro with kernel_pin and larger window, post perf captures here. assigning self to root-cause, pinging @mike for telemetry queries and @kevin for kernel heuristics patch. :hammer:

mike: noted, will pull raw traces and correlate spans (toolcall_id).

kevin: I'll prototype a small heuristic: if kv_eviction_rate > 0.1 && recent_tool_loop > 0.05 -> bias to fastpath kernels (avoid recompile). will schedule a quick experiment.

sara: test results (first run): kernel_pin=true -> p99 reduced from 320ms -> 140ms. batch_window=20ms -> p99 ~180ms. combined -> 120ms. obvious win but need to check throughput drop.

ana: throughput tradeoff expected. what's CPU/GPU utilization change?

sara: GPU utl was +5% when kernel_pin, CPU scheduler wait dropped. throughput down ~8% at peak.

mike: sounds reasonable as a mitigation. next: can we do a canary with kernel_pin for 10% of traffic and collect SLO regressions?

sara: will do. creating canary now -> canary id: canary-1952-kernel-pin. will post results in ~30m.

kevin: FYI I also pushed a small logging flag to annotate requests that trigger recompile so we can sample the offending inputs.

infra-bot: canary canary-1952-kernel-pin started at 03:54 (10% traffic) :rocket:

ana: thanks team. if we confirm the tool-loop + kv-evict -> recompile pattern, we'll add a regression test in perf suite and a monitor on kernel_recompile_rate vs kv_eviction_rate.

sara: one more note: some outlier generations include base64 payloads from upstream service, massively increasing sequence length unpredictably. adding input sanitizer to cap tokenized length to 2048 for small-gen route as a protective guard.

mike: good catch. add a log + metric when truncation happens so we can alert developer owners.

sara: will follow up with PRs: 1) canary observations, 2) kernel heuristic proto, 3) input sanitizer for small-gen.

kevin: thanks, will review kernel heuristic PR. :+1:

sara: closing for now, will update when canary finishes. :eyes:
